meta.title: Math workbench
meta.description: A full-page workbench organized by book and chapter. Open it from its sidebar icon: a book card opens the book's chapter list, a chapter row expands in place, and the breadcrumb or the Back button returns to the shelf. Books and chapters come from 索引.json when it exists, otherwise from the chapter-split PDF file names under the library directory (default ~\数学书库, configurable); PDFs that are not chapter-named are skipped and listed in the page footer. An expanded chapter offers Open PDF and a double-click shortcut; both explain that the built-in PDF reader is not wired yet. The chapter also shows its sessions in three groups (Extract / Q&A / Exercises) matched by the title `[<book> cNN] <mode>`, each group with its own New button: a session is created in the Workspace that owns the library and appears in its group as unsent; its title is written when the first message is sent, and unused blanks are archived on the next workbench visit, so they neither linger nor lend their name to another session. New first continues that chapter's existing conversation in the group, and only starts a numbered continuation (`（续 N）`) once its context is near the window (85% by default, configurable as resumeRatio); a conversation's native chapter is named by its title prefix, so importing it into another chapter adds a placement without changing where it came from. Each group also has Import, which attaches an existing conversation to the chapter (marked ↪) without changing its title; ✎ renames a row inline and × detaches only that chapter, and one conversation can sit under several chapters while its title still names its primary chapter. Clicking a session opens the host conversation. Titles that match no chapter or mode are counted in the footer, which also shows where sessions are created and the book-id legend. The open book, the last chapter used and each book's expanded chapters are stored on the Host, so they return after a reload and scroll back to that chapter. The chapter also lists its produced files (directory `产物/<book id>/<cNN>/`; the empty state prints the full path and offers a copy button): a text-like file (md/txt/tex/code/json/csv, …) opens the workbench's own preview on the right, with line numbers and up to 512 KB, and truncation and encoding stated above the text; Escape, ×, or the backdrop closes it and returns focus to the row; other binary files open the same drawer with a note. Files are not noticed automatically: click Reload in that section after adding one, and a collapsed chapter row still shows its file count. Double-clicking a chapter, its Open PDF button, or a PDF produced file opens the built-in reader (pdf.js) inside the workbench, with switchable single-page and continuous modes: previous/next, a page box to jump, zoom out / fit width / zoom in, ↑↓ to scroll, ←→ and PageUp/PageDown to turn pages, +/− to zoom, Escape to exit; continuous mode paints pages near the viewport only. The reader toolbar also carries the chapter's three ＋ buttons (Extract / Q&A / Exercises): one creates a session and jumps to it, opening this chapter's PDF on that session's right side (hideable, expandable to full screen); returning to the workbench reopens the reader on the same page and mode. Page data is served over loopback only.
